video_title: Micah Nori Postgame Interview | Trail Blazers 123, Warriors 118 | Oct. 7, 2026

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the Trail Blazers' defensive struggles and turnovers
quotes.excerpt: we're too good of a defensive team to get into a trading baskets type thing
quotes.quote: I think Danny did a good job getting himself downhill, but we're too good of a defensive team to get into a trading baskets type thing. But that being said, we sat in here and talked about the very first thing is we want to take care of the basketball and we want to rebound, and we gave them 34 extra possessions. So, 12 offensive rebounds, 22 turnovers, you're just not going to win or survive in the NBA with that.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says the Trail Blazers cannot survive in the NBA after giving up 34 extra possessions through turnovers and offensive rebounds. You are just not going to win or survive in the NBA with that.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori evaluates Ja Morant's performance and rustiness
quotes.excerpt: he just looked a little bit rusty
quotes.quote: I think that he was just sped up. I think he was just sped up and I think some of it was timing issues. I even think he started rough. I think he had the very first play of the game, had Donovan open at the rim and just under-threw the lob. But with four turnovers, and then I think when he went into the paint, I don't know, he had a hard time finishing. I don't know if he might have got hit, might not have, but I just think he just looked a little bit rusty.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on Ja Morant after a 4 turnover performance: I just think he just looked a little bit rusty.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Ja Morant's aggressive paint-attacking mentality
quotes.excerpt: we don't want to deter that mentality
quotes.quote: The one thing that's great is like he's always looking to throw ahead, he's always looking to push the ball. I think he got where he wanted to go, it just that he either wasn't able to convert and kind of got himself stuck under the rim. But the one thing we don't want to do is tell him not to go in there. We don't want to deter that mentality because I do believe Ja Morant, once we get going, if he stays in that type of attack mode, getting himself downhill, playing with pace, looking to throw ahead and get others involved, that's going to benefit us.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says the team wants to keep Ja Morant in attack mode despite some early struggles. We do not want to deter that mentality because if he stays in that type of attack mode that is going to benefit us.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori explains the decision-making process for point guard duties
quotes.excerpt: if the five-man gets it, they're looking for Ja
quotes.quote: Some of it depends on if it's off of a rebound. If it's a rebound, we've told our guys basically one through four, if any of those guys get it to push. If the five-man gets it, they're looking for Ja. Now that also means that if the five is looking for Ja, but Dame is open or Danny is open on a throw-ahead, kick it up to them of course. On a make, the clock is moving, it's the same way. If Ja or Dame are right there, they can grab it, they both know what we're trying to do.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori explains the Trail Blazers transition philosophy: If the five man gets it they are looking for Ja. Now that also means that if the five is looking for Ja but Dame is open or Danny is open on a throw ahead kick it up to them.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Scoot Henderson's transition play and pace
quotes.excerpt: he's been phenomenal in camp is playing with the pace
quotes.quote: I think Scoot, same way like all of them. It's kind of like you're sitting there and you're just training, training, training and then you just say sprint and you're seeing all this. So I think the one thing that him that we've always talked about and he's been phenomenal in camp is playing with the pace but then playing under control with that pace. And then just a couple of times he got himself into a little bit of trouble, he contributed to the turnovers things as well, but 3-for-8 for him, 1-for-3, 2-for-2 from the line, he's competing.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori on Scoot Henderson: The one thing that we have always talked about and he has been phenomenal in camp is playing with the pace but then playing under control with that pace.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori praises Hansen's offensive hub role and defensive effort
quotes.excerpt: Hansen came in and did exactly what we need him to do
quotes.quote: I think Hansen came in and did exactly what we need him to do. I thought that he had a pretty good feel for the offense. We played a lot through him as the hub. He made a lot of good decisions, was able to finish around the basket, and did even a good job. I think the one thing that you've been harping on with Hansen is his defense and playing in the drop. And I thought he did a pretty good job. He kept the ball in front of him, he challenged, and then he tried to get back and rebound.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori praises Hansen for his role as an offensive hub and his defensive effort in the drop. I thought that he had a pretty good feel for the offense. We played a lot through him as the hub.
